verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.243
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.243

verses.pali: 25. Āpattibhayavagga
verses.english: 25. Perils of Offenses

verses.pali: Saṅghabhedakasutta
verses.english: Schism in the Saṅgha

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “api nu taṁ, ānanda, adhikaraṇaṁ vūpasantan”ti?
verses.english: “Well, Ānanda, has that disciplinary issue been settled yet?”

verses.pali: “Kuto taṁ, bhante, adhikaraṇaṁ vūpasamissati.
verses.english: “How could it be, sir?

verses.pali: Āyasmato, bhante, anuruddhassa bāhiyo nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṁ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito.
verses.english: Venerable Anuruddha’s protégé Bāhiya remains entirely committed to creating a schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Tatrāyasmā anuruddho na ekavācikampi bhaṇitabbaṁ maññatī”ti.
verses.english: But Anuruddha doesn’t think to say a single word about it.”

verses.pali: “Kadā panānanda, anuruddho saṅghamajjhe adhikaraṇesu voyuñjati.
verses.english: “But Ānanda, since when has Anuruddha been involved in disciplinary issues in the midst of the Saṅgha?

verses.pali: Nanu, ānanda, yāni kānici adhikaraṇāni uppajjanti, sabbāni tāni tumhe ceva vūpasametha sāriputtamoggallānā ca.
verses.english: Shouldn’t you, together with Sāriputta and Moggallāna, settle all disciplinary issues that come up?

verses.pali: Cattārome, ānanda, atthavase sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
verses.english: A bad monk sees four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Katame cattāro?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idhānanda, pāpabhikkhu dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo asuci saṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto.
verses.english: Take an unethical monk, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: He thinks:

verses.pali: ‘sace kho maṁ bhikkhū jānissanti—
verses.english: ‘Suppose the monks know that I’m a bad monk …

verses.pali: dussīlo pāpadhammo asuci saṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujātoti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
verses.english: If they’re in harmony, they’ll expel me,

verses.pali: vaggā pana maṁ na nāsessantī’ti.
verses.english: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

verses.pali: Idaṁ, ānanda, paṭhamaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
verses.english: A bad monk sees this as the first reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato.
verses.english: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong view, he’s attached to an extremist view.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: He thinks:

verses.pali: ‘sace kho maṁ bhikkhū jānissanti—
verses.english: ‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong view …

verses.pali: micchādiṭṭhiko antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
verses.english: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,

verses.pali: vaggā pana maṁ na nāsessantī’ti.
verses.english: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

verses.pali: Idaṁ, ānanda, dutiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
verses.english: A bad monk sees this as the second reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu micchāājīvo hoti, micchāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong livelihood and earns a living by wrong livelihood.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: He thinks:

verses.pali: ‘sace kho maṁ bhikkhū jānissanti—
verses.english: ‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong livelihood …

verses.pali: micchāājīvo micchāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappetīti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
verses.english: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,

verses.pali: vaggā pana maṁ na nāsessantī’ti.
verses.english: but if they’re divided they won’t.’

verses.pali: Idaṁ, ānanda, tatiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
verses.english: A bad monk sees this as the third reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu lābhakāmo hoti sakkārakāmo anavaññattikāmo.
verses.english: Furthermore, a bad monk desires material things, honor, and admiration.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: He thinks:

verses.pali: ‘sace kho maṁ bhikkhū jānissanti—
verses.english: ‘Suppose the monks know that I desire material things, honor, and admiration.

verses.pali: lābhakāmo sakkārakāmo anavaññattikāmoti, samaggā maṁ santā na sakkarissanti na garuṁ karissanti na mānessanti na pūjessanti;
verses.english: If they’re in harmony they won’t honor, respect, revere, or venerate me,

verses.pali: vaggā pana maṁ sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessantī’ti.
verses.english: but if they’re divided they will.’

verses.pali: Idaṁ, ānanda, catutthaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
verses.english: A bad monk sees this as the fourth reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Ime kho, ānanda, cattāro atthavase sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandatī”ti.
verses.english: A bad monk sees these four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
